title: Revealing Intrigue and Building Novelty
coreMove: Pace revelation so curiosity stays alive and the room keeps trying to resolve the tension.
sourcePressure: Intrigue chapter: novelty and surprise keep the audience mentally active when they sharpen curiosity and consequence without becoming confusion, theater, or empty hype.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer must make intrigue meaningful and sequenced, not clickbait, confusion, or hype for its own sake.

hook: Curiosity is the currency of attention

exampleSpecs.domain: space-hardware supplier pitching a vibration isolator to satellite integrators
exampleSpecs.audience: a hardware lead whose product looks like a small bracket until consequence is revealed
exampleSpecs.stakes: one launch vibration mode can destroy a payload worth years of work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she shows a slow-motion test clip paused one second before failure and asks which part the room thinks breaks first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paused vibration-test video above a foam-lined metal case

exampleSpecs.domain: opera company development director pitching a youth-access fund to estate lawyers
exampleSpecs.audience: a fundraiser who must create curiosity without sentimental overload
exampleSpecs.stakes: lawyers file the program as ordinary arts outreach unless the hidden demand pattern emerges
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he begins with the unopened ticket envelope from a student waitlist, then reveals the number of similar requests only after the room guesses
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cream ticket envelope sealed with a student name tag

exampleSpecs.domain: commercial diving trainer selling a simulator module to offshore safety managers
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainer whose safety record can become a flat compliance recital
exampleSpecs.stakes: managers miss the near-miss pattern the simulator was built to expose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he lets the first thirty seconds of helmet-camera footage run without explaining what went wrong, then freezes on the missed gauge
exampleSpecs.firstImage: helmet-camera footage glowing on a waterproof monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: artisan textile exporter pitching a traceability platform to luxury buyers
exampleSpecs.audience: an exporter who needs novelty tied to provenance, not gimmick packaging
exampleSpecs.stakes: buyers treat the platform as a QR-code accessory instead of margin protection
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she lets buyers handle two identical scarves, then scans only one tag to reveal the dye-house chain and counterfeit risk
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two indigo scarves laid across a black lacquer table

exampleSpecs.domain: pediatric sleep clinic pitching a remote coaching program to benefits brokers
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician with outcomes data that can flatten into wellness noise
exampleSpecs.stakes: brokers miss the employer cost of exhausted parents taking leave
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she starts with one voicemail transcript stopping before the parent says why she missed work, then reveals the leave total after brokers infer the problem
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a voicemail transcript clipped to a benefits-cost sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: ceramic tile manufacturer pitching crack-resistant material to subway maintenance planners
exampleSpecs.audience: a materials rep who must make a small design change feel consequential
exampleSpecs.stakes: planners keep replacing cracked station tile during overnight windows
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he drops a cracked sample and an intact sample from the same height, but waits to name the material difference until the planner asks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two tile squares resting on a rubber mat under fluorescent station lights

skillTargets: choose what to reveal and what to withhold
evaluate when surprise has become empty theater

tryThisNowSpec: Find one fact you usually explain immediately and write the question or visible test that would make the room want that fact first.
